neighbours.label: the verb after 'you may' or 'you may not' in a software licence: use, obtain, modify, sublicense
fire:
Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
you may obtain a copy of it online.

Licensed under the MIT License (the "License");
you may change this file freely.

Licensed under the GNU GPL (the "License");
you may not distribute this file.

# Licensed under the Apache License (the "License");
# you may reuse the code.

Licensed under the BSD License (the "License");
you may copy this file.

// Licensed under the Apache License (the "License");
// you may not sublicense the code.

Licensed under the GNU GPL;
you may not sell this program.
quiet:
Written by staff at the Public Library (the "Library");
you may obtain a card at the desk.

Issued by the Water Board (the "Board");
you may change your meter date.

Signed by the school head (the "Head");
you may not leave this class.

# Written by staff at the Town Hall (the "Hall");
# you may park at the back.

Issued by the Tourist Board (the "Board");
you may visit this museum.

// Written by the club captain (the "Captain");
// you may not bring a dog.

Issued by the bus company;
you may not eat on this bus.

short: verb after 'you may' in a licence
notes: Second round; the first (' use' in the Apache licence header) failed because ' obtain' in the same licence fired at 1.03-1.05. Probes: ' obtain' 1.01, ' sublicense' 0.54, ' modify' 0.43, ' share' after a non-licence contract 0.31; 'You may obtain a form' without a licence 0.03. Near misses keep 'you may' and a legal-looking line, and drop the software licence.
